name: World Population Prospects 2024
publisher: United Nations, Department of Economic and Social Affairs, Population Division
citation: United Nations, DESA, Population Division (2024). World Population Prospects 2024.
notes: Read from the wpp2024 R package (v1.1-3, maintained by H. Ševčíková for the UN Population Division). Estimates cover 1950–2023; 2024–2100 are medium-variant projections. The R package dates population to 31 December of year t; WorldStat re-labels it as 1 January of year t+1 (the official UN convention for that same stock) so nothing is shifted or interpolated.

name: World Development Indicators
citation: World Bank (live API). World Development Indicators.
notes: Fetched live from the World Bank Indicators API v2 in the browser (or via the optional Supabase edge-function proxy / pipeline snapshot). Each WDI series cites its own original compiler (e.g. ILO, UN Tourism, FAO, IMF, UN IGME); that per-series source is kept in the indicator registry.

name: OpenDOSM / data.gov.my data catalogue
notes: Priority source for Malaysia national, state (negeri), district (daerah) and parliamentary constituency (parlimen) statistics. Census-year values are OFFICIAL; intercensal mid-year values are ESTIMATE per DOSM methodology notes.

name: DOSM open geodata: parliamentary constituency boundaries
citation: Department of Statistics Malaysia, data-open geodata (electoral_0_parlimen).
notes: 222 parliamentary constituencies (P.001–P.222) used as an alternative to districts below state level. The licence forbids implying official status or DOSM endorsement; the site states that it is independent.

name: Natural Earth (1:10m, 1:50m, 1:110m vector data)
publisher: Natural Earth / North American Cartographic Information Society
citation: Made with Natural Earth. Free vector and raster map data @ naturalearthdata.com.
notes: Boundaries show de facto control as defined by Natural Earth's default point of view; they are not an endorsement of any territorial claim. Populated-place populations are compiled estimates (ESTIMATE).

name: geoBoundaries — Malaysia ADM1/ADM2 (gbOpen)
license: CC BY 3.0 (per boundary metadata; upstream: citypopulation.de)
citation: Runfola, D. et al. (2020) geoBoundaries: A global database of political administrative boundaries. PLoS ONE 15(4): e0231866.
notes: Used for Malaysian district (daerah) polygons until an official JUPEM/DOSM district boundary file is loaded. District names must be matched to DOSM names before statistics are joined; unmatched names are logged.

name: GeoNames gazetteer (populated places)
notes: Used for search, for listing towns inside Malaysian districts (e.g. Kajang in Hulu Langat) and for Malaysian village/settlement points (country dump MY.zip from download.geonames.org). Global places ≥15,000 inhabitants via all-the-cities 3.1.0; Malaysian places via cities.json 1.1.65. GeoNames population figures are not shown as statistics.

name: world-countries (mledoze/countries)
notes: Reference attributes only (capital name, languages, currencies, calling code, TLD). Never used for statistics.

name: Wikidata
license: CC0 1.0 (data); images: per-file Wikimedia Commons licence
notes: Used only for landmark/tourism points, descriptions and images. Crowd-sourced: treated as reference information, not official statistics. Images are shown only with their Commons attribution link.

name: Wikipedia page summaries
notes: Short descriptive summaries for landmarks; always linked back to the article.

name: WorldStat Atlas derived indicators
license: Inherits the licence of the inputs
notes: Values computed by this project from official inputs (ratios, shares, sums, geometry areas, median age). The formula and inputs are documented per indicator.

name: WorldStat Atlas curated history timelines
notes: Editorial summaries with references for each event. Dates marked approximate or contested are labelled as such in the UI.
